entities.summary:
Autobiographical work by saint augustine Created by Augustine of Hippo.

Written between 397-401 CE, Confessions is a deeply personal and philosophical exploration of spirituality, morality, and the human condition. Through vivid narratives and introspection, Augustine grapples with his past, his faith, and his relationship with God.

This work not only offers insight into the life and thoughts of one of Christianity's most influential figures but also has had a profound impact on Western literature and philosophy.

Its legacy can be seen in the countless works of writers, theologians, and philosophers who have followed in Augustine's footsteps, exploring similar themes of identity, morality, and the search for meaning.
